name: Long Island Sound Community Impact Fund (LISCIF)
summary: Community-driven grants, run with EPA and the Long Island Sound Partnership, for habitat restoration, pollution reduction, resilience and stewardship projects in the New York and Connecticut Long Island Sound watershed.

geography.label: Long Island Sound watershed (New York and Connecticut)

eligibility.rule: Incorporates Actions of the Comprehensive Conservation and Management Plan
Completes the project in the LIS region, or serves qualifying CT and NY communities for outreach and education
Addresses common challenges and LISCIF Funding Priorities
Is not a federal agency, except as a partner in an eligible recipient's proposal
Does not primarily conduct research or monitoring, except to assess grant-funded results

documents: General location map, unless the project is region-wide
Potential partner organizations list with role descriptions

geography.quote: Up to $1,200,000 in competitive funding will be awarded to support projects in New York and Connecticut.

window.quote: This is the fourth round of LISCIF funding.

effort.quote: Letters of Intent (LoIs) are Due: November 20, 2026, by 4:00 pm EST.
RAE will request a Full Proposal from qualifying applicants

eligibility.quote: Projects must incorporate Actions of the Comprehensive Conservation and Management Plan (CCMP).

Projects funded under LISCIF must be completed within the LIS geographic region (see region map: https://estuaries.org/liscif/)or, in the case of outreach and education, include communities in Connecticut and New York that use the Long Island Sound for recreation, sustenance, or economic activities.
Applicant activities and projects funded under LISCIF must address common challenges and the priorities identified above under "Funding Priorities.
Federal agencies are not eligible recipients of funding but may be included as partners in proposals submitted by eligible recipients.

LISCIF27 will not fund proposals in which the primary purpose is research or monitoring; however, research and monitoring may be funded as part of a larger grant, where the purpose of the research or monitoring is to assess results and outcomes of the grant-funded activity.

after_award.quote: Grantees must submit quarterly progress reports as well as a final report.
RAE conducts periodic on-site audits of financial records and programmatic progress of all grantees.
Grantees will be required to participate in an Annual Learning Exchange meeting during the period of the award, to be held within the LIS region.

documents.quote: A map or maps of the proposed project area is required for all proposals except those which are region-wide in scope. Attach a single PDF file, standard letter size, 3 pages max., 10 MB max. List of Potential Partner Organizations with brief descriptions of roles
A budget table is also required of all proposals.
